items.title: Lyn Alden: one-person risk undercuts a mega cap's value
items.takeaway: Alden says investors pay a premium expecting mega caps not to hinge on one person. Either tech and scale are the moat, or it is flimsy.
items.soWhat: Boards should test whether their moat survives without the person at the top.

items.title: Claude-built C beats Rust in Simon Willison's SQLite test
items.takeaway: An optimized C extension ran at 16 to 19 ns per row, about twice as fast as the Rust versions, and all matched across 8 million fuzz checks.
items.soWhat: Agents make it cheap to build and benchmark two designs before you commit to one.

image.alt: Simon Willison: Claude-built C beats Rust in Simon Willison's SQLite test

items.title: Nvidia board opens independent probe into Jensen Huang
items.takeaway: Independent directors and outside counsel will review Huang's relationship with a Megaspeed executive. The board says it sees no compromise of secrets.
items.soWhat: The leading AI chip supplier now carries key-person and export-control risk at once.

related.name: The Verge: full text of Jensen Huang's memo to Nvidia

items.title: Cursor's poteto shares skills that map an app's state machines
items.takeaway: In pstack, /create-formal-verification-skill models state machines per subsystem and /statechart visualizes key user flows.
items.soWhat: Agents can now map the hidden logic in your app before they change it.

items.title: Apple pushes to ship a Siri that acts inside apps
items.takeaway: Per Bloomberg's Gurman, Ternus is pressing Federighi to speed Siri up. First-party app control is expected with iOS 27.3, third-party apps likely in spring.
items.soWhat: If Siri can order and book inside apps, customers may stop opening yours.

items.title: Patrick Collison: the upside case for AI is still unclear
items.takeaway: Collison asks what the good AI equilibrium looks like beyond cured diseases and abundance: who works, what is scarce, who is in control.
items.soWhat: Without a clear upside story, public debate about AI stays stuck on data centers.

items.title: Elvis and Eminem rights holders sue Suno over AI imitations
items.takeaway: The Presley suit cites Tennessee's ELVIS Act on voice cloning. Suno says it blocks artist-name prompts and screens uploads.
items.soWhat: Voice-cloning laws are turning into real legal exposure for anyone shipping generative media.

items.title: Open-source WebGL recreation of the MacBook Pro wallpaper
items.takeaway: kubai087/pro-threads is an MIT-licensed WebGL animation of letters woven from light threads, with a full A to Z typeface and palettes.
items.soWhat: Polished motion backgrounds are now free building blocks for product and launch pages.

items.title: Swyx says Cursor ended 2025 at $1B in annual revenue
items.takeaway: Swyx posts that Cursor ended 2025 at $1B ARR with enterprise growing 300% quarter over quarter. He cites a screenshot; not checked against filings.
items.soWhat: Treat it as a claim until filings confirm, but enterprise coding-tool spend looks strong.

items.title: Google's Tulsee Doshi on how frontier models actually get built
items.takeaway: Lenny Rachitsky interviews Google's head of product for frontier models on evals versus vibes, writing a first eval, and her 60-20-20 shipping framework.
items.soWhat: Frontier labs still lean on product judgment and evals, not just engineering, to ship models.

items.title: Musk says Grok Bot token efficiency fixes are underway
items.takeaway: Musk says fixes are underway after a user reported a $200 plan that lasted seven days now lasts 14 hours. Matt Palmer is collecting feedback.
items.soWhat: Usage-priced agent plans can shrink fast, so track what your team actually gets for the money.

related.name: Musk reply on the $200 plan report

items.title: Vitalik Buterin: a data center slowdown looks net good
items.takeaway: Vitalik argues algorithmic progress lets today's data centers match bigger ones within about four years, buying time to harden against cyber and bio risks.
items.soWhat: Opposition to data centers now has a capability-neutral case that investors and boards will hear.

items.title: Addy Osmani: managing coding agents is managing a team
items.takeaway: Osmani maps manager habits onto Claude Code: give agents a way to check work, write down what is not in the repo, treat hooks as hard rules, plan first, review diffs.
items.soWhat: Teams get more from agents by managing them well than by writing clever prompts.

related.name: Osmani essay: coding agents need a manager

items.title: Kun Chen's /headless skill sets up always-on agent machines
items.takeaway: /headless walks an agent through turning a Mac, Linux or Windows box into an always-on SSH machine without seeing the admin password.
items.soWhat: Dedicated agent machines are getting easy to set up without handing agents admin credentials.

items.title: Greg Isenberg's playbook for building iOS apps with agents
items.takeaway: Find low-rated, high-revenue utility apps, cluster 1-2 star reviews with an agent, then build with Claude Code, the Xcode plugin and simulator MCPs.
items.soWhat: Apple's Xcode plugin is already turning into repeatable app-building playbooks for small teams.

items.title: Perplexity Teammate automation runs grew 3.7x on day two
items.takeaway: Srinivas says runs grew 3.7x from launch day to a Friday, crediting a code-first harness, model neutrality and search quality. No absolute counts.
items.soWhat: Early workplace agent demand looks real, but growth ratios without base numbers prove little.

items.title: AWS runs Claude Code as a remote agent on AgentCore
items.takeaway: AWS published a sample that runs each Claude Code task in an isolated AgentCore session in your AWS account and returns a GitHub pull request.
items.soWhat: Remote coding agents can now run inside your own cloud boundary, away from laptop credentials.

image.alt: Image from AWS Machine Learning Blog

items.title: Claude Agent SDK guard hooks fail open unless set to block
items.takeaway: Agent SDK for Python 0.2.177 adds on_failure on HookMatcher. The default, continue, lets a crashed guard hook allow the tool call.
items.soWhat: Teams relying on SDK guard hooks should set on_failure to block, or a buggy guard becomes a hole.

items.title: MaxxBench: coding models tied at 74% split by 23 points
items.takeaway: MaxxBench mutates 89 DeepSWE tasks. Spread across 15 configurations widens from 20.9 to 48.3 points; authors report reward hacking and a sandbox bypass.
items.soWhat: Pick coding agents on how they handle changed requirements, not on headline benchmark ties.
